steps.text: This place will no longer shelter you.
Begone, dear warrior. Turn about and flee. Your pitiful destiny is already set in stone. You have no place in this world any longer.
Indeed, your existence has no meaning for us anymore.
......Thus, the warrior fled. She, who never once trembled in fear under the thundering of the enemy's drums, who never faltered against the roars of her cruel opponents, turned and ran.
Akroti, a region in Minos bordering Sargon, comprised of many villages
Days of unending rain would sicken even the most tenacious of young warriors.
Not to mention this pitiable fellow, sunken to the darkest depths of despair.
What sort of experiences would have forced her to leave her home at such a young age?
What happened to her, such that her heart would ache in sadness whenever she looks back at her homeland?
She wishes no one to know.
Go on, flee. Head to that unknown land.
Yet——
What's the situation?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Just stopped moving. She's been struggling there for two hours already, moved about ten meters since we found her.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: If she really was a competent spy, she'd be playing dead to conserve her energy instead of drawing our attention like this.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: It could also all be an act, to play on the Minoans' sympathy and lower their guard.
Yes, the Minoans would have trouble ignoring such a weight on the conscience. What do you think of this foreign warrior, and what she's done?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Hmph, just a trick.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: She's definitely acting. You know it's Sargon's fault, their tricks and lies, that these villages took so long to...
That's a different conversation. I want you to take a closer look at her. Set aside your suspicions and look at her, see her innocence.
I appreciate your concern for the villagers' safety.....

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: (Sneer)
Whether it comes from a good place or not. You need only tell me, warriors of Sarkaz, how fares the outsider now?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: In short, she's at death's door.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Looks like she was crossing over from Sargon, judging by her weapon and equipment. Now, she just looks like a fish out of water, struggling helplessly on Minoan soil.
Is she alone?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: So far, she is... Though that might change later.
Hmm, if that's the case...

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Hey, Priestess, 'Pallas'.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: It's not my job to say what's what, but since the Minoans hired me and appointed you to take command, I'll just remind you—

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: You're not a normal nurse, but neither are you a naive priestess who knows nothing but sympathy and forgiveness.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: You're the commander of the Minoans, mentor to the budding warriors, the so-called 'Goddess' worshipped by all these Minoan villages.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: If you take her in, everyone must treat her with the same amount of respect and devotion that they give to you. After all, you were the one who found her.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Yet this little warrior is, without the slightest hint of doubt, of Sargon——

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Until there is peace with Sargon, she remains an enemy to Minoans, one they have to stay wary of.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Warrior, your words carry your intentions well, and reveal the breadth of your knowledge. I listen out of respect and duty.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: But as you know, there exists a divide between your judgment and mine. It is a saddening reality, but it is one we must face.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I am indeed considering taking her in, and treating her wounds at the least.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Hers is a young life, one hanging by a thread. And I believe she means us no harm.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: As for whether thousands of Sargon's soldiers lurk behind her shadow, that is for you to determine.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: In the absence of danger, we may not fall upon the ongoing war as an excuse to abandon another's life.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: (How pointless.)

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Some may think this a pointless act. That is why I let the others return to their duties, while you remain here, watching over her.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Sarkaz, oh poor Sarkaz. Your callous demeanor is known far and wide, and you rely on it for survival. In other words, many among you take pride in your indifference.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: One must heel to one's proficiencies. I give my orders based on this principle.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You need only ensure your mission is completed. As for other matters... they will be resolved, one way or the other.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Since you refuse to change your mind even after listening to me, wouldn't it be the same if someone else was looking after her?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You've been working as a mercenary here for three months now. I'm sure you're aware of the situation.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: If it were left to the Minoans, this would be over in ten minutes, much less two hours. Their guilt would gnaw at those pure hearts of theirs, bidding them to lend a hand, regardless of the danger...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: In such a scenario, how badly shaken would those sincere hearts of theirs be, if that betrayal really came to fruition?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Hah. In the end, even you admit that those villagers are way too soft-hearted, to value the life of a potential enemy.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I understand you, Sarkaz. Some of the villagers have accepted you, and the elders view you as one of our own. You have their goodwill to thank for that.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: However, your needs do not lay there. Between love, or at least this love that exists between we of different races, and the payment of money that you receive, you do not believe that it is worthless.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: There's nothing to discuss about that.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You live life your own way, and I have never questioned that.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: But I think that Sarkaz demeanor I mentioned——perhaps you were like that, once. When we first met, you harbored a kindness not altogether pure, and a heart not completely vile.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Yet, that has changed. Your interactions with the Minoan soldiers and the villagers have spurred your thoughts. You have become an intelligent warrior brandishing your weapon of your own free will.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Your vigilance is warranted. It's just that I believe Sargon has no reason to attack right now, and neither is there a need to use such crude 'bait.'

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Rather than formulating a trap to prey on others' kindness, the Sargon's troops would be far more willing to march in brashly, declaring their cruel intentions to plunder and slaughter for all to hear.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Right, right. Let's just go with what you said.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: For now, let us turn our eyes to this young warrior who's wandered over from Sargon.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Just as you said, though I wish to save her...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Just as you warned, it would be far from prudent to simply bring her back to the villages.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: She has no visibly open wounds, and it does not seem to be any complex disease that would require surgery.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I will attempt to treat her wounds. The consequences of this will be mine to bear.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: You mean you want me to put up a tent here, so you can treat her wounds? In this place not even two kilometers from the border? Even the garrison is farther away!

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Well, there's not much difference with the garrison anyway...

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Don't forget your place. You're the villagers' beacon of hope, the one who will free them from the threat of Sargon.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: They love you, and call you the 'Goddess of Victory', yet here you are taking such risks...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Watch your words, soldier.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: ...Tch.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: A young woman whose guilt is yet unproven, who has waited for over two hours, struggling to keep herself awake, all for the sake of survival.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: She has already passed your test——As the keenest and most vigilant Sarkaz, you are unable to bring out solid evidence of her duplicity.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: And so, my heart is already filled with guilt. I cannot bear to leave her any longer.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: I don't object, if you really insist on it. But... it's hard to say if that girl will even talk to you like this after she wakes up.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Just be prepared for an attack once she wakes up.
At this moment, the young Sargon warrior is suffering in her dreams.
She drags her body onward with naught but sheer determination, but in the end her vision disappears in a fog of darkness.
As she loses herself within the rest that has long eluded her, she is wrapped in a blanket of warmth. Yet, this warmth is unfamiliar to her, and she remains vigilant even in her dreams.
Thus, she escapes from her dreamland, escapes the trap of comfort, escapes the warm touch on her skin.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Ah. You're awake?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Calm down. You've been sleeping for quite a long time...
The Kuranta soldier immediately rises, swiftly inspecting her surroundings.
The narrow space contains only herself, the Forte woman and some scattered items.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: ...I understand. You're looking for your weapon, yes? Here it is.
The Kuranta soldier snatches the weapon. With seemingly no hesitation, she swings the flail towards the Forte.
The narrow space limits her movement. The weapon catches on the surrounding canvas, making a dull thud.
The Forte woman remains at the bedside, without a trace of surprise on her face.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Decisive and orderly moves. Mystery woman, I can tell you are a well-trained soldier, confident in your own strength.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Unfortunately, this place is not fit for combat.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: Answer my questions, and do nothing else, or my flail and shield will smash you... *cough*

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Alright, alright. I shall do naught but answer your questions, till you're satisfied.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: Where are we?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: In my tent. To treat your injuries, a place of rest is needed.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: Save it! Where is this tent? Who else is here?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Our soldiers, Minoans.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: (Al'ama, how did I end up with the Minoans?)

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You arrived from Sargon, collapsing on the Minoan side of the border. When the soldiers found you, you were still determinedly inching forward.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: This is... Minoan land?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I've packed your possessions, they're by your feet.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You must have been extremely hungry and tired, not being aware that your compass had malfunctioned as you struggled to make your way here and that all your navigation equipment was damaged.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: As you can hear, there are only Minos soldiers outside. You are alone, and it would be unwise to force a discussion using violence.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: This would depend on the manner in which you wish to leave this tent. We may come to an agreement and you can leave this tent assured of your safety. You may also refuse to negotiate and leave immediately, foolish as that may be.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: Can you prove that?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I am a priestess. The villagers and soldiers will follow my orders, out of respect to their faith.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: I know well enough to know none of that is true.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: This place is in the midst of a war with the tribes of Sargon. If your home isn't far from here, you should have heard of this.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: We are... near Akroti?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Absolutely.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Well then, visitor of Sargon. How may I address you?

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: Don't ask.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Oh? This is a rather unfair exchange then, at least in regards to me.
The Kuranta soldier furrows her brows, as if trying to clear her thoughts and scrutinize her situation.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: Just now, you said that after I fainted on Minoan land, you'd been treating my injuries all this while?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Compared to the cold interrogation you would face with the soldiers, there may at least be a chance to come to an agreement with me instead.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: An agreement?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: An agreement with you, young Sargon soldier.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Appearing suddenly by the border, hungry and disheveled, with no trace of any pursuit. I had come to the conclusion that, perhaps, you were not, in fact, an enemy at all.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: I recall that the lord ameer here doesn't have a particularly good reputation.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: The war is between you and them, don't drag me into it. I'm just passing through.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Aha, as I thought! In that case, pray lower your weapon, innocent one. I wish for a conversation between equals here, at least until I have fully expressed my sincerity.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: You... You're pretty hard to understand, with the way you speak.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Oh? The warriors complain about it from time to time, but it has never been my intention. In fact, I used to be called the most approachable priestess in the Hall of Heroes...

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: In any case, I don't want to meet your soldiers, officers, or anyone really. I'm no longer in service to Sargon anyway.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: I just want to leave, quickly. I don't really care about anything else.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Alright, alright. If so...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Hmm.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Innocent warrior, young as you are, you have bravely traversed the dense forest to arrive here. Will you not lay down your weapon and have some food?

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: I'm fine... Ugh...!

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Don't waste your energy standing up. You need not worry, for I am the village's priestess, and will only be helping to treat your wounds here.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Until we come to an acceptable agreement and leave this tent, neither I nor those outside will act against you.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: I've already said that there's nothing to discuss.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: (I can't bear it, I'm too hungry...)

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Please sate your hunger, unnamed traveler. Though your weapon remains pristine, your body is overly taxed. It would be unbearable to one such as you, who trains strictly in the path of the warrior.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You may not have had much interaction with Minoans prior, or you may have merely heard rumors. In Minos, our soldiers take neither a single step forwards nor backwards until ordered.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I do request your understanding, as some precautions still need to be taken against you during this period of wartime. It's just that the Minoan soldiers are all extremely polite...

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: Why'd you save me then?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: It's probably an ingrained virtue, as we sometimes allow objective and rational decisions to accommodate kindness still.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: Then, what is that weapon there for?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Ah... Yes, you wield a similar weapon to mine, of course you would notice.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: I knew it...!

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: No, please allow me to explain. Firstly, innocent guest, your weapon appears to be of exceptional craftsmanship. I believe it is the work of an esteemed Sargon craftsman.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You must have cherished and trained with it often, so, please look... I believe you can determine how this weapon of mine has been used, or perhaps how proficient I really am.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You see, just as you harbor suspicion towards me, so too did I doubt your identity.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: But, just look at you now! Your deep exhaustion is etched on your face, and both your equipment and supplies have been run as ragged as you are.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Most importantly, your weapon shows no signs of recent damage. You have not been in a battle for quite some time. Based on this, I have no reason to fear you.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: So in the end... we're still gonna fight.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Oh, definitely not! I will not be using that as a bargaining chip in our discussion. In fact, I will lay my own weapon on the floor.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Observe! Dear traveler from Sargon, please feel free to partake in this nutritious food. I am fully convinced that you are unrelated to our true enemies.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: In consideration to your current state, this free and delicious meal should not be left for too long, regardless of any choice you may make later on.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Oh, finally out huh.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: Sarkaz...

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: What, my horns alone enough to scare you?

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: You...!

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: That look of fear and disgust... I've been judged at a glance too damned many times.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I seek your forgiveness, brave warrior. Your existence is not at fault.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Hmph, I'm sure you think so, priestess. But what about her? She won't listen to you.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: I... Priestess, you said that there were Minoans standing guard outside.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: They went for lunch a while time ago. They'll probably be drinking wine, singing and reciting poetry right after too, so they got me to help stand guard here.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Ah, it appears that my admonishments were still not taken seriously. I had wanted to show you the magnanimity of the Minoan soldiers...

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: Probably better this way.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: I'll be leaving immediately. I don't want to loiter around your battlefield.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Oh? Are you leaving now, fearless traveler?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: The famous village of Akroti is but a stone's throw away. You might find it worth your while to pay a visit.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: E-Even if there are theaters and cinemas? There's also a really good Minoan restaurant...

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: No. Thank. You.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: *sigh* There's also our warriors' favorite baths...

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: ...Bath?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Forget it. Mixed gender bath.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: No way.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Y-You can also use the small bath reserved for the priests. For a traveler on such a long and weary journey as you, taking a well-deserved rest is...

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: I said no! I... I'm not traveling.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: It's better if I'm not seen. I have a bad feeling about this, I'm leaving.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: We're still too close to Sargon.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Ahh... But, it's so rare to see so rustic and pitiful a foreign youth...

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Ignore her. It's been a long time since she left the big city she used to live in. She's probably going insane from having to stay in this backwater for so long. It's pretty amazing you can stand that tone of hers.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: The villages of Akroti are not safe for you. If you are running from something and want to avoid trouble, you should probably leave now.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: However, foreigner, where lies your destination? To be traveling in such a harried state, could it be that you committed some unspeakable crime, or perhaps insulted an important noble?

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: No, I'm just... a mercenary... and I'm free.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: My destination doesn't matter, as long as I get further away.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: To the north, and further to the east. This place... I will not survive long here.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: Deserts, battlefields, Sargon... I don't want to face any of these right now.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Ah... A pitiful youth who shoulders the terrible weight of her painful past.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Please at least leave your name, so that I may pray for you, whether it be strength to face the dangers ahead or guidance to the place you may find happiness.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: Are these prayers any good for people from Sargon?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Heh. I don't believe in it, for what it's worth.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: (Stomps on his foot)

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: *Hiss*... Pallas...!

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: 'Pallas'?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: (*sigh* The blame for exposing me lies with you, Sarkaz warrior.)

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: It is not a name worth remembering, at least for now.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Although, there are such stories——On the border of Minos, a priestess bears the revelations of the twelve heroes, arriving to protect the honor and freedom of the Minoans, taking up the fight against Sargon's invasions and always able to clutch victory from the jaws of defeat...

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: Never heard of them.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: *cough*—*cough* *cough*... W-Well, I suppose the war has not yet been won.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Apologies, I had no intention of declaring that name. I only hope that these myths of Minos may spread to Sargon as well, such that we can come to understand each other better.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: You should save those words for the next visitor from Sargon passing by.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: *Sniff*... Fine. It seems that besides wishing you well, there is nothing else we can do for you, traveler from Sargon.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I will gift you this working compass.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Though you know not where you are going... You must continue moving onwards. That is the only goal you have now, and the only way to escape your suffering.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: To move onwards is a choice, one most miraculous. I believe that you will receive much help on your journey, traveler.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: When the next kindly person appears, one who can devote their energies to you, one who can save you from the most dangerous of mountains, one who can help you escape the clutches of Death... You may make your choice then, or even decide to accompany them.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Hey, watch out, priestess. What if those sufferings you just mentioned really happened to her?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: The things you say are oddly profound, at times.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: Forget it... it doesn't really matter.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: Maybe the destination of this journey is the journey itself.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I will pray for you, young lady. The road you tread stretches far, very far indeed.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You are a warrior. A brave, persevering warrior. Your bravery is etched on your weapon, etched on your limbs, etched in your very soul itself.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Though your eyes are hazy now, a strong rain will wash it all away and your vision will be clear once more.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I apologize for not being able to devote myself to the task of earning your trust. We all have the same, more important things to do.

steps.name: Heavyrain
steps.text: I'm still suspicious of you.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You, me, and that adorable Sarkaz warrior. We are all on a journey without a destination, struggling and suffering to move onwards for the sake of our souls, even as we seek that one thing we must experience, that most important thing——

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: To find a place for ourselves.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Hey, time to change shifts.

steps.name: Minoan Soldier
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Minoan Soldier
steps.text: Hey, Sarkaz.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Minoan Soldier
steps.text: Shouldn't you tell us your name by now? Or do you really want to go by 'Sarkaz'?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: A name's just a name. You call your priestess 'Goddess'. She calls herself 'Priestess Pallas'. Does that really make her so?

steps.name: Minoan Soldier
steps.text: Whatever. Though, after we win this war, the only name you'll be leaving to the legends would be 'Sarkaz' then?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Hah, let's see if we even survive! You're pretty confident, Minoan!

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: (It's not really important whether I'm hailed as a hero in history.)

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: (As long as I'm a Sarkaz, as long as I'm treated as a Sarkaz no matter what I do...... It's not too bad to be fighting alongside heroes.)

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Priestess Pallas, what are you doing here?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Ah, Mister Sarkaz.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Don't call me that. Why are you standing night watch? Did something happen?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Not something to mobilize the masses, I hope.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: It's just that today's events have been weighing heavily on me. I have had an urge to come here, to find the answers I seek.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: What, are you still thinking about that Sargon Kuranta soldier? What's so special about her?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: No, it's exactly the opposite. She's normal through and through.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: She's normal, yet she hurries along, as if running away from some evil spirit while keeping everyone at arm's length.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: She does not seem predisposed to such behavior. I would presume that a great change has occurred recently, one that has left her despondent.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Mister Sarkaz, what do you think could have happened?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: No idea. I don't share your interest in going through people's life stories.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: I only need to know what you're doing here. You act as if you want me to do something, while also looking like you're just loitering around. Tell me what's on your mind, mercurial 'Goddess'.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Shh.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: (Grabs his blade)

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Who's there?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: It's just as you said, Mister Sarkaz. It's difficult to discern one's heart, and my fateful encounter with our Kuranta visitor was sadly lacking in depth.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Even so, you and I have witnessed her fragility——Her fortitude is bent and broken, and she is at her most vulnerable right now. There isn't much we can do for her, with a good breakfast being the greatest courtesy we can confer.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Even so, even so. That poor Kuranta soldier. Her only pursuit right now, is the power to grasp her own fate. To choose a destination of her own, or to end it on her own terms.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: No matter what, she possesses the same goal as ourselves. To search for freedom, that is our mission.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Try as I may, I am unable to imagine how vile it must be, that evil spirit behind the loss of her freedom. I never believed I would face such a saddening scene.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Ah, 'Mister Sarkaz', do you weep for such a tragedy?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: As things are now, perhaps I should make my warning clear in advance, so that the approaching battle will reach a more direct conclusion——

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Malign one, you are different from the earlier traveler. Your body reeks of the stench of blood and evil. You have a cruel plan, and the target is one much weaker than you.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You wish to carry out a murder, a hunt, a dirty plan to brag about, upon this holy land of Minos. This, I will never allow.
Without warning, a shadow leaps out of the dark night and rushes towards the Minoan priestess.
In an instant, his attack is blocked by an opposing blade.
The attacker immediately falls back.

steps.name: Sarkaz Assassin
steps.text: Stand aside, my kin. This obnoxious priestess who keeps rambling on about inane topics annoys me.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: It seems that you didn't understand her words, which is to say you don't know why she's so unhappy right now.

steps.name: Sarkaz Assassin
steps.text: I have my own task. I believe it should have nothing to do with you.

steps.name: Sarkaz Assassin
steps.text: She seems to want to stop me from finding a 'Kuranta soldier.' I can see that she's been anticipating a battle since before I tracked the clues here.

steps.name: Sarkaz Assassin
steps.text: Since she wants to protect my target, she must die. What are you doing here then?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: I'm working as a soldier, helping the Minoans here.

steps.name: Sarkaz Assassin
steps.text: Ah, we are not enemies then. We both have a job to do, so let's go our own ways.

steps.name: Sarkaz Assassin
steps.text: Is that witch's life part of your responsibilities?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: That's not something you need to think about.

steps.name: Sarkaz Assassin
steps.text: Indeed. Every swing of my blade has a price, and I have no reason to waste my energy here.

steps.name: Sarkaz Assassin
steps.text: ——Unless, that absurd speech of hers has displeased me. Maybe I want to drag her horns along, to point a faster path to that Kuranta soldier.

steps.name: Sarkaz Assassin
steps.text: I haven't guessed wrongly, have I? Witch.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: What an uncultured and ill-manned beast.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You view yourself as a dirty blade and refuse all counsel. Is that really the case?

steps.name: Sarkaz Assassin
steps.text: *spits* That's enough. Kinsman, I have no quarrel with you. Close one eye and leave, if you know what's good for you.
The assassin prepares to strike at the priestess. However, the mercenary steps in front of her, not moving an inch.

steps.name: Sarkaz Assassin
steps.text: Oh, what's this? You're a Sarkaz, do you really think that you'll be treated as an honored bodyguard, with nothing but the blessings of the Minoans?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Nothing to do with the priestess. I just think that you've lived a really sad life.

steps.name: Sarkaz Assassin
steps.text: Don't tell me you've never done such things. Frankly, you're no match for me.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Nay, ruthless intruder, wicked pursuer. It is because of that blind arrogance of yours that you will lose.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Heroes do not await death meekly. Moreover, heroes do not stand aside as monsters chase their prey about.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Blinded by money and power as you are, you have already forgotten how shameful it is to persecute and kill.

steps.name: Sarkaz Assassin
steps.text: Whatever you say. If you really have the stuff, I'll stop after cutting off one of your horns.

steps.name: Sarkaz Assassin
steps.text: To be honest, I think my talents are being wasted on a simple deserter. Wouldn't I get a nicer reward if I brought back a Minoan head?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Since you have cursed and insulted me so, I no longer hold the slightest bit of remorse for that devil-bewitched heart of yours.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: For the sake of that Kuranta traveler's safety, I will not let you leave alive, cruel assassin.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Pitiful, tragic Sarkaz warriors. Your once chaotic hearts are no longer the same. You have each stepped on vastly different paths.

steps.name: Sarkaz Assassin
steps.text: There's only one ending for Sarkaz. Salvation does not exist. Just shut up, witch. Here I come——
This battle in the dark night was never recorded in the annals of history.
Some souls continue running, becoming ever purer in their journey of life.
In time, they will shine with the brightest light.
In time, these sparks of light will gather about the traveling Rhodes Island, becoming a glorious blaze that moves ever onwards.
